clue.text: One retrieving game: a new Man City player

parts.note: a gundog is trained to fetch shot birds for the hunter
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dog that fetches game is mixed up with a new signing at Manchester City football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes the first half look like a description of the player; it is a dog. Ilkay Gundogan is a German midfielder who captained Manchester City.
explanation.definitionFit: Gundogan played in midfield for Manchester City, the English Premier League football club, so he is one example of its players.

clue.text: Star from Greece with character there above dress circle

indicators.note: in a down entry one part sitting above another simply comes earlier in the reading

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greece
eta is a letter of the alphabet used in Greece, a character from there
garb is clothing, dress
O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A Greek actress sits in the theatre's upper tier, the dress circle, watching a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress circle' reads as a single theatre phrase but splits into two pieces. 'There' points back to Greece, so the character is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood screen legend of the silent and early sound era, a film star.

clue.text: American with Pole in for training beat Italian

indicators.note: training puts something through drills that reshape it, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
taken as written
taken as written
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: An American and a Polish athlete, in training together, manage to beat their Italian rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like the verb of the sentence but supplies letters of its own: tan, as in giving a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, a southern city, so the word describes one kind of Italian person.

clue.text: Maybe G8 leaders to end talks after month

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed later in the reading order

parts.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October

indicators.note: leaders stand at the front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Heads of the G8 nations try to wrap up their summit negotiations once the month is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The G8 summit picture is a decoy: the definition reads G8 as 'group of eight', and 'Maybe' signals that this is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is any set of eight, and the G8 was a group of eight nations, so it is one instance.

clue.text: Answer for alien's reserved but planned in advance

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep something held back, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
taken as written
ET is the film alien
'though' can mean 'but', as in 'it's fine, though'

explanation.surface: Someone explains that an extraterrestrial seems shy but had actually rehearsed every word beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien's reserved' reads as a description of a shy alien; the 's is 'has', so the alien has kept 'but' tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforethought means premeditated, as in the legal phrase malice aforethought, describing something deliberately arranged beforehand.

clue.text: Little woman with bottle full of spirit?

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women
a vial is a small glass bottle

explanation.surface: A small woman clutching a bottle of liquor, presumably well topped up with spirits herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' looks like any short woman, but it is a sister from Little Women. The question mark admits the definition puns on spirits as drink in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means cheerful and lively, high-spirited; the clue also hints at a bottle containing alcohol.

clue.text: 1-0 up: hard supporter's throttled Reds fan?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: one-nil, with nil as the letter O

indicators.note: throttling grips something round the neck, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a pile is a post supporting a building; the 's is 'has'
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A Liverpool fan, with the Reds leading one-nil, is so tense they are half-strangling the supporter next to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The football setting makes Reds sound like Liverpool or Manchester United; it means red wines. Liverpool's nickname is the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and connoisseur of wine, so someone who enjoys red wines qualifies, punningly, as a fan of reds.

clue.text: Bird single for second time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
bis is Latin for twice, used in music and in addresses for a repeat

explanation.surface: A bird goes solo for the second time, as if releasing another single record.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is the term called out for an encore or printed in scores for a repeated passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading species with a downcurved beak, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Seconds in plenty with beef put in place

indicators.note: seconds are things in second position, so the letter after the first is taken from each word

parts.note: its second letter
its second letter
its second letter
its second letter

explanation.surface: Second helpings of plenty of beef are served up and put in their place on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' suggests second helpings at dinner; it means second letters. 'In place' echoes the phrase 'in lieu', meaning instead of.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu is French for spot or position and survives in English chiefly in 'in lieu of', meaning instead.

clue.text: Demand made in divorce court case?

parts.note: a divorce leaves you with an ex
a legal action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A claim lodged during a divorce hearing, the sort of financial demand a spouse makes in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The divorce-court picture is apt, but the definition sits apart: divorce gives one piece and the court case another.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is the act of requiring payment or effort, often harshly, so it is a formal demand.

clue.text: Stimulate understanding for an audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so it is the spoken sound of the word that counts

parts.note: insight is deep understanding

explanation.surface: A lecturer aims to provoke real comprehension among the people listening to the talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Insight and the answer are pronounced alike in most accents, though spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or provoke someone into action, close in sense to stimulating them.

clue.text: Heard Pilsner interfered with randy men

indicators.note: interfering with something messes it about, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone's lager was spiked by a group of lecherous men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' tempts toward a sound-alike clue, but here it is simply part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Philanderers are men who chase women for casual affairs, so lustful womanisers, which is what randy men are.

clue.text: Last pope and his troubled role in the Church

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and unsettled, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historian reflects on the final pontiff and his anguished position in the Catholic hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The papal picture keeps attention on the Church, which is where the answer also sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostleship is the office or mission of an apostle, a founding position of leadership in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Decline note taken round Russian city once denied power

indicators.note: taking one thing round another means wrapping it about the outside

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: to be denied something is to go without it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: the name St Petersburg bore from 1914 to 1924
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A message is carried around a former Russian city whose electricity has been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Petrograd was the city's name between St Petersburg and Leningrad, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, retrograde means to go backwards or deteriorate, so it can stand for decline.

clue.text: Maths expert's lager tab is recalculated

indicators.note: a recalculation works the figures out again, so these letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mathematician at the pub has to total up the bar bill for beer a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An algebraist is a mathematician specialising in algebra, so a specialist in one branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Ace team needs order in principle

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A top-class side must, as a matter of principle, keep good discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests discipline but is a royal honour, the OM, awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as self-evidently true and used as a starting basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Rough and ready fashion garment

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it
a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: A crude, hastily thrown-together piece of clothing from the fashion world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a noun about clothing but works as a verb meaning to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift describes something improvised as a temporary substitute, crude but serviceable, which is what rough and ready means.

clue.text: Pop star one entering auditorium successfully

indicators.note: entering means just coming through the door, so the next piece follows straight on

parts.note: a concert hall is an auditorium
I is the Roman numeral one
doing something well is doing it successfully

explanation.surface: A singer makes a triumphant entrance into the concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice of the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Halliwell had a string of chart hits both with the Spice Girls and as a solo singer, making her a famous chart singer.

clue.text: Jet stream in northern location

parts.note: jet black, as jet is a black stone
a burn is a Scottish and northern word for a stream

explanation.surface: A weather report: the jet stream is sitting over the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet stream' reads as one meteorological term but splits in two. Blackburn is a town in Lancashire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackburn is an industrial town in Lancashire in the north of England, so it is a place up north.

clue.text: Far side of the lake is spooky

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: its final letter
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: The opposite shore of the lake, seen through the mist, has an unsettling ghostly feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far side of the lake' looks like a single scenic phrase; the far side belongs only to 'the', and the lake is a named one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening in a ghostly or uncanny way, which is a synonym of spooky.

clue.text: School crooner bored by the French director

indicators.note: something bored is drilled into, so another piece is driven into its middle

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a crooner is a soft-voiced singer
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A crooner at a school concert sends the French audience to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' wants to mean weary of the singing, but it means drilled into. John Schlesinger was the British director of Midnight Cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Schlesinger directed films such as Midnight Cowboy and Darling, so he is a film director.

clue.text: Here in Paris monarch is more aloof

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: On a visit to France, the visiting king or queen is noticeably more distant than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Latin for Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy manner is cold and unfriendly, so icier describes someone even colder and more distant.

clue.text: Still avoiding eastern desert

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping clear of it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: still means calm and silent
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A traveller still keeps away from the eastern stretch of the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun for sandy waste; it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place or post is to leave it for good, so to abandon it, as a soldier deserts.

clue.text: Area of filled pizza having no calories

indicators.note: having none of something means it is gone, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a calzone is a folded, stuffed pizza
cal is the abbreviation for calories

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders where to find a stuffed pizza that has no calories at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The dieting picture hides that the abbreviation is cut from the start of the pizza's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a district or region marked off for a purpose, so a distinct area.

clue.text: More work's work one placed in out-tray occasionally

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside
something done occasionally happens now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters
OP is short for opus, a work, and I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An office worker gets yet more work: another job dropped into the out-tray now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More work' looks like extra labour, but More is Sir Thomas More, and the 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is the 1516 book by Thomas More describing an ideal island society, his best-known work.

clue.text: One Tibetan animal in rite cooked as food

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the yak is the long-haired ox of Tibet
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Tibetan animal is cooked during a religious ceremony and served as a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked as food' reads as one phrase; 'cooked' belongs to the wordplay and only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese dish of meat or fish glazed in sweet soy sauce, so a kind of cuisine.

clue.text: Score from left in play when ball's thrown out?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
something thrown out is discarded, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
O is round like a ball; the 's is 'is'
left as the past tense of leave, meaning departed

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what does the batting side score from the left once the ball is chucked away?
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting picture hides that 'left' is a verb in the past tense and 'Score' is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old word for a set of twenty, as in 'three score years and ten'.

clue.text: Voracious French FA in time exploit backing

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
going backwards means the letters run from right to left

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to exploit something is to use it
sweet FA (Fanny Adams) is British slang for nothing; rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A greedy French football association seizes the moment to take advantage, supporting its own interests.
explanation.walkthrough: FA looks like the Football Association, but in 'sweet FA' it is British slang for nothing at all, which French renders as rien.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a rare literary word meaning hungry or greedy, a close synonym of ravenous.
